analysis:
Only provider-swift/Tests/DarkbloomCLITests/SandboxSetupTests.swift changed. It is test-only and adds no production code or runtime attack surface. Base units 2 and 3 are the prior file. Head unit 4 covers head lines 1-456. The newest tests are in the later head lines of the diff (up to roughly 821), but only lines 1-456 were visible, so the remainder was not reviewed.

What the added tests exercise, relevant to TB-013 and T-061:
- SandboxInstaller.planArguments produces ['--plan','--json-progress', slots] with no --yes. The plan is a dry run that does not auto-confirm (head 125-130).
- supportsPlan detects whether the downloaded installer script supports --plan.
- SandboxSizingPlan parses the installer's JSON 'plan' event. It accepts schema 1 only, ignores unknown members, and rejects missing members or other event types (head 189-211). This is a fail-closed parser for untrusted installer output.
- The planReport and verdict tests cover eligibility display.
- The background/waitsInBackground tests check that approval and waitlist events set 'background' only when the value is a real boolean, and that other stages' 'background' values are ignored (head 175-187, 361-384).
- The advice tests check the exit-status messaging.

Existing installer-validation tests are unchanged and remain in the file. They cover https-only URLs, userinfo, query and fragment refusal, a 1 MiB cap, a shebang check, and an owner-only staging mode of 0700/0600 (head 52-142). They assert the TB-013 and T-061 mitigations rather than weaken them.

Open question for the next pass: the production implementations of the plan/--plan execution path, SandboxSizingPlan, and the background-wait advice are not in this batch. Whether the plan run executes the downloaded script before any user confirmation is unverified. If it does, it runs the installer as the owner earlier than the confirmation step, and that needs review against T-061. The tests alone do not show this, so no finding is raised.
